A UI kit is the drop-in lane of an SDK: the screens a product needs to gate itself on a license, from boot and sign-in to devices, updates and settings. Every kit draws the same component catalog with the same theme API, copy catalog and flows, so a person moves between your app, Polaris Locker and the console in one system. The other lane, [your own UI](/docs/start/choose-your-integration/), draws the screens itself.

**Requires:** an SDK with a kit, and its [quickstart](/docs/start/choose-your-integration/). [All frameworks](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/) lists each kit and whether it is built.

## Two lanes

Each SDK's quickstart forks after the shared setup into two lanes.

- **Drop-in screens.** The kit, whole or piece by piece: the gate, the sign-in form, devices, updates. The sign-in form's `presentation: "browser"` hands the whole flow to the Locker sign-in card in the browser, with no UI code.
- **Your own UI.** Your screens drawn over the SDK's headless layer, on the SDK's own-UI page ([Node](/docs/build/sdks/node/your-own-ui/), [React](/docs/build/sdks/react/your-own-ui/), [Python](/docs/build/sdks/python/your-own-ui/), [Swift](/docs/build/sdks/swift/your-own-ui/), [Kotlin](/docs/build/sdks/kotlin/your-own-ui/), [Godot](/docs/build/sdks/godot/your-own-ui/)).

## Three layers in every kit

Every component in the [catalog](/docs/build/ui/components/) has three layers, so a team can drop in a flow, restyle a component, or rebuild the UI on the state alone:

- **(a) The drop-in flow:** one call that gates the app and runs every screen it needs.
- **(b) The styled parts:** each screen and each part on its own, themed, with slots.
- **(c) Headless:** the state machine, its actions and its copy keys, with no UI.

A kit's [framework page](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/) names the API it ships for each layer. Layer (c) is one state machine in every language, checked against shared fixtures.

## The look

- **The Polaris Key look by default.** A kit renders the brand's surface, text, status and elevation tokens, Rubik, and the radius and motion tokens. It is dark first with light parity and a System, Dark and Light choice.
- **In the product's accent.** Polaris violet appears only when you ask for `accent: "core"`. Every accent goes through one contrast resolver, so buttons, links and the focus ring stay legible in both themes ([Theming](/docs/build/ui/theming/#the-accent-resolver)).
- **Or the host's look.** The `native` preset keeps the structure, flows, copy and spacing and hands color, type and materials to the host ([Theming](/docs/build/ui/theming/#the-native-preset)).

`pnpm ui:lint` checks the hard rules for a modern UI: no boxed forms, no heavy borders, no stock alerts or spinners, visible states and tokenized motion.
